scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO develops a new generation of AI agent architectures grounded in neuro-symbolic planning with verifiable reasoning, persistent and adaptive memory, and decentralised multi-agent coordination, unified by an External Tool and API Orchestration Layer

MAESTRO develops a hybrid neuro-symbolic planning engine combining LLM-based reasoning with formal symbolic planning methods to decompose high-level goals into executable sub-task graphs with formally specified pre-conditions, post-conditions, and verification checkpoints

MAESTRO designs a unified adaptive memory architecture integrating working memory, episodic memory (retrieval-augmented store of past task episodes), and semantic memory (persistent knowledge graph of domain concepts and tool capabilities), managed by a memory controller

MAESTRO develops formal decentralised multi-agent coordination protocols enabling heterogeneous agents to negotiate, decompose tasks, delegate subtask assignments, establish shared commitment structures, and resolve resource conflicts with provable convergence guarantees

MAESTRO develops an External Tool and API Orchestration Layer providing a typed tool registry with capability models, formal tool selection and invocation policies, standardised API adapters abstracting heterogeneous protocols (REST, GraphQL, HL7 FHIR, OPC-UA), post-invocation verification and result validation, execution monitoring with fallback/recovery, and auditable tool execution traces

MAESTRO validates through a Healthcare clinical decision support demonstrator using HL7 FHIR API integration for patient data gathering, planning differential diagnoses, and coordinating specialist sub-agents for imaging analysis and lab result interpretation (call-identified Apply AI sector)

MAESTRO validates through an Advanced Manufacturing process optimisation multi-agent demonstrator using OPC-UA industrial connectors, digital twin APIs, and sensor data streams to autonomously monitor, diagnose, and optimise manufacturing processes (call-identified Apply AI sector)

MAESTRO includes a Logistics and Supply Chain Operational Resilience demonstrator as a cross-sector transfer demonstrator, explicitly described in the concept note as being beyond the call's specifically identified Apply AI sectors (healthcare, advanced manufacturing, in-vehicle autonomous driving)

The MAESTRO architecture's transferability to in-vehicle autonomous driving settings — requiring real-time multi-agent coordination, sensor APIs, V2X communication, and verified planning under safety constraints — is assessed through a targeted architectural mapping analysis in WP8
MAESTRO allocates dedicated tasks for cohesion activities with the European Partnership on AI, Data and Robotics (ADRA) and with the GenAI4EU central Hub (CSA HORIZON-CL4-2025-03-HUMAN-18)

All research outputs — frameworks, models, benchmarks, the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, and demonstrator results — will be shared with the European R&D community through the AI-on-demand platform
The project links to resources offered by AI Factories and Data Labs for compute-intensive training and evaluation
Demonstrator results will be validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities and disseminated via European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
MAESTRO incorporates qualitative and quantitative KPIs, standardised benchmarking across all demonstrators, and structured progress monitoring at 6-month integration checkpoints
Research activities target TRL 5 by project end, validated in operational environments across call-identified Apply AI sector demonstrators

scope_findings.flag_reason: Constraint CC-14 (maximum 48-month project duration) has status 'Assumed' in call_constraints.json, with an explicit assumption_note stating the 48-month maximum is not present in the topic text (call_entry) and that verification against Tier 1 General Annex B is required. The MAESTRO project duration of 48 months is exactly at this assumed maximum ceiling. The claim cannot be confirmed as definitively in-scope until CC-14 is elevated from 'Assumed' to 'Confirmed' through Tier 1 General Annex B verification. Scope boundary authority is Tier 2B only per constitutional constraint; the assumed status of the underlying constraint creates a traceability gap that must be resolved before this claim can be treated as confirmed compliant.

scope_findings.claim: The strategic positioning document attributes the portfolio priority sector requirement (healthcare, advanced manufacturing, in-vehicle autonomous driving) to 'SR-07'
scope_findings.flag_reason: The strategic positioning document labels the portfolio priority sector preference requirement as 'SR-07', but SR-07 in scope_requirements.json defines TRL activity boundaries (research scoped between TRL 2 at project start and TRL 5 at project end), not sector preferences. The sector preference requirement is SR-11. The mislabeling creates a false Tier 2B requirement reference in a Tier 3 project document and will mislead downstream traceability checks that follow the SR-07 reference. The underlying sector claim is factually supported by SR-11 and CC-09. This traceability inconsistency must be corrected in the Tier 3 strategic positioning document (CLAUDE.md §10.5).

scope_findings.claim: The strategic positioning document identifies 'CC-10' as the portfolio coverage mechanism designed to ensure at least one funded proposal per sector
scope_findings.flag_reason: The strategic positioning document labels the portfolio coverage mechanism as 'CC-10', but CC-10 in call_constraints.json defines Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) provisions (maximum €300,000 per third party at grant stage 2, etc.), not portfolio coverage. The portfolio coverage mechanism is CC-09. This mislabeling creates a false constraint reference in a Tier 3 project document. The underlying portfolio coverage claim is factually supported by CC-09. The Tier 3 document reference must be corrected to CC-09 to preserve constraint traceability (CLAUDE.md §10.5).
